recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up FHIR core source work is needed unless a future work-group decision changes exists discriminator semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-31603 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution requiring the exists slicing documentation to state that there can be no more than two slices, differentiated by one slice with max 0 and the other with min 1 or more, and that declaration order does not matter.
initial_application: The request was applied by Jira-tagged commits b0ca47c034 and c7b89199bb on 2022-08-21. The former updated the ElementDefinition discriminator-type code definition in source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml, and the latter updated the profiling narrative in source/profiling.html.
additional_context: The current combined-branch source still contains the requested wording in both source/profiling.html and source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml. ElementDefinition is active in source/fhir.ini, and profiling.html is linked from active conformance and documentation pages. Confluence minutes for the 2021-07-12 FHIR-I call record FHIR-31603 as Persuasive with Mod, and targeted Jira/Zulip/Confluence searches found no later conflicting decision.
reconciliation: No source edits were made. The current source already explains that exists slices are differentiated by presence or absence of the nominated element, that there SHALL be no more than two slices, that one has max 0 and the other min 1 or more, and that slice declaration order does not matter.
